==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|mărʹē|a=RP,GA}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈmæɹi/}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-ne-marry.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈmɛəɹi/|a=US,Mary-marry,CA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-marry.ogg|a=US,Mary-marry}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈmæɹi/|a=AU}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈmɛɹi/|a=NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈmaɾe/|/ˈmaɾɪ/|a=Scotland}} * {{homophones|en|Mary|;|Merry|merry}} * {{rhymes|en|æɹi|s=2}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|marien}}, from {{der|en|xno|marïer}}, from {{der|en|la|marito|marītāre|t=to wed}}, from {{m|la|marītus|t=husband, suitor}}, from {{m|la|mās|t=man, male}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. Possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*méryos||young man}}, same source as {{cog|sa|मर्य|tr=márya|t=suitor, young man}}. Compare its feminine derivatives: {{cog|cy|morwyn||girl}}, {{m|cy|merch||daughter}}, {{cog|gme-cgo|marzus||wedding}}, {{cog|grc|μεῖραξ||boy; girl}}, {{cog|lt|martì||bride}}, {{cog|ae|𐬨𐬀𐬌𐬭𐬌𐬌𐬀|t=yeoman}}.J.P. Mallory and D.Q. Adams, ''Encyclopedia of Indo-European Culture'', s.v. "woman" (London: Dearborn Fitzroy, 1997), 656.) Displaced native {{ncog|ang|hīwian}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To enter into the [[conjugal]] or [[connubial]] state; to take a [[husband]] or a [[wife]]. {{defdate|from 14th c.}} #: {{synonyms|en|[[get]] [[married]]|wed|Thesaurus:marry}} #: {{antonyms|en|divorce}} #: {{ux|en|Neither of her daughters showed any desire to '''marry'''.}} #: {{ux|en|I forfeited my inheritance and '''married''' outside my parents' faith.}} #*: Evelyn, in his "Diary," under date 1641, says that at Haerlem "they showed us a cottage where, they told us, dwelt a woman who had been married to her twenty-fifth husband, and, being now a widow, was prohibited to marry in future; {{...}}" #* {{quote-book|en|year=1755|title=The Holy Bible, both Old and New Testament, Digested, Illustrated, and Explained|section=second edition, page 59 |passage=But ''Esau'', being now forty years of age, took a false step by '''marrying''' not only without his parents consent; but with two wives, daughters of the ''Hittites''.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=March 17 1975|author=Marian Christy|title=Suzy Chaffee, A Liberated Beauty|journal=The Lebanon Daily News |passage=If and when Suzy does '''marry''', it will be an [[open marriage]] because she's a believer in the "totality" of freedom.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To enter into [[marriage]] with one another. #: {{ux|en|Jack and Jenny '''married''' soon after they met.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To take as husband or wife. {{defdate|from 15th c.}} #: {{ux|en|In some cultures, it is acceptable for an uncle to '''marry''' his niece.}} #* {{quote-av|en|year=2008|title={{w|Xavier: Renegade Angel|Xavier: Renegade Angel}}|season=1|number=10|text=First Xavier ({{w|Vernon Chatman|Vernon Chatman}}): You're about as deep as a bowl of soup, and your tongue is as sharp as a soup spoon.
Second Xavier ({{w|Vernon Chatman|Vernon Chatman}}): Hey, say what you want about me, but lay off the soup.
First Xavier: If you love soup so much, why don't you '''marry''' soup?
Second Xavier: 'cause I'm already married. To justice.
First Xavier: Yeah. Only a blind girl would '''marry''' you.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To arrange for the [[marriage]] of; to give away as wife or husband. {{defdate|from 14th c.}} #: {{ux|en|He was eager to '''marry''' his daughter to a nobleman.}} #* {{RQ:Tyndale NT|Matthew|22|2|xxx|verso=1|text=THe kyngdom̃ of hevẽ is lyke vnto a certayne kinge / which '''maryed''' his ſonne{{nb...}}.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1810|author={{w|Edward Forster (writer)|Edward Forster}}|title=w:The Arabian Nights|location=London|publisher=William Miller|volume=V|page=170|passage=[T]o this son he gave the shop of Cassim, with a further promise, that if he continued to behave with prudence, he should, ere long, '''marry''' him advantageously, considering his situation in life.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|title=Mr. Vivian A. Webber on “Population and Emigration.|journal=w:[[Isle of Wight Observer#Earlier title|The Isle of Wight Observer]]|issue=931|location=Ryde, Isle of Wight|date=2 July 1870|page=5|pageurl=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/396449387/|column=3|passage=The Queen has set the example of '''marrying''' her children very early in life; {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To unite in wedlock or matrimony; to perform the ceremony of joining spouses; to bring about a marital union according to the laws or customs of a place. {{defdate|from 16th c.}} #: {{ux|en|A justice of the peace will '''marry''' Jones and Smith.}} #: {{ux|en|His daughter was '''married''' some five years ago to a tailor's apprentice.}} #* {{RQ:John Gay What D'Ye Call It|scene=ix|pages=38–39|pageref=39|passage=What ſhall the Curate controul me? Have I not the Preſentation? Tell him that I will not have my Play ſpoil'd; nay, that he ſhall '''marry''' the Couple himſelf—I ſay he ſhall.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To acquire by marriage. #: {{syn|en|marry into}} #: {{ux|en|I wanted to '''marry''' wealth and power, and got both.}} # {{lb|en|figurative}} To devote oneself to so as to occupy one's life; to substitute (something) as a marriage partner. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1955|year_published=1959|author=w:Ian Fleming|title={{w|Moonraker (novel)|Moonraker}}|volume=|location=London|publisher=Pan Books|chapter=Secret Paper-work|page=unbroken7|passage=She was tall and dark with a reserved, unbroken beauty to which the war and five years in the Service had lent a touch of sternness. Unless she married soon, Bond thought for the hundredth time, or had a lover, her cool air of authority might easily become spinsterish and she would join the army of women who had '''married''' a career.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|figuratively|of inanimate or abstract things}} To [[join]] or [[connect]]. ''See also '''[[marry up]]'''.'' #: {{ux|en|There’s a big gap here. These two parts don’t '''marry''' properly.}} #: {{ux|en|I can’t connect it, because the plug doesn’t '''marry''' with the socket.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|figuratively}} To unite; to [[join]] together into a close union. {{defdate|from 15th c.}} #: {{ux|en|The attempt to '''marry''' medieval plainsong with speed metal produced interesting results.}} #* {{RQ:King James Version|Jeremiah|3|14|passage=Turn, O backsliding children, saith the Lord; for I am '''married''' unto you.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=Lisa C. Hickman|title=William Faulkner and Joan Williams: The Romance of Two Writers |passage=For Faulkner, these years '''marry''' professional triumphs and personal disappointments: the Nobel Prize for Literature and an increasingly unlifting depression.}} # {{lb|en|nautical}} To place (two ropes) alongside each other so that they may be [[grasp]]ed and [[haul]]ed on at the same time. # {{lb|en|nautical}} To join (two ropes) end to end so that both will pass through a [[block]]. =====Derived terms===== ===Etymology 2=== From {{inh|en|enm|Marie}},{{R:Merriam Webster Online|marry}} referring to [[Mary]], the [[Virgin Mary]].{{EtymOnLine|marry}} Mid-14th century. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|mary#Interjection}} ====Interjection==== {{en-intj}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} {{non-gloss|A [[term#Noun|term]] of [[asseveration]]}}: [[indeed]]!, [[in truth]]! #* {{RQ:Latimer Lords Prayer|part=2|chapter=Edward VI 7|folio=93|passage=You that be of the court, & eſpecially ye ſworn chaplains beware of a leſſon that a great man taught me at my firſt coming to the court he told me for a good will, he thoughte it wel. He ſayd vnto me. You muſt beware how ſo euer ye do that ye cõtrary not the king, let him haue his ſaiyngs, folow him, go with him. '''Mary''' out vpon this counſel, ſhal I ſay, as he ſayes?}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 4-2|act=I|scene=ii|passage=I have chequed him for it, and the young lion repents; '''marry''', not in ashes and sackcloth, but in new silk and old sack.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Othello Q1|act=II|scene=i|page=24|passage=I know too much: / I finde it, I; for when I ha liſt to ſleepe, / '''Mary''', before your Ladiſhip I grant, / She puts her tongue alittle in her heart, / And chides with thinking.|translation=I know, [she talks] too much: / I always find that when I have the desire to sleep. / '''Indeed''', before your Ladyship I admit / She keeps a little quiet, / And scolds me with her thoughts.}} ===See also=== * {{l|en|wed}} ===References=== {{reflist}} ===Further reading=== * {{pedia|Marriage}} {{cln|en|ergative verbs}} {{cln|en|reciprocal verbs|eponyms}} {{C|en|Marriage}}
